Work with H3 local IJ coordinates

Source: R/h3_local_ij.R
ddbh3_local_ij.Rd

Convert H3 cells to local IJ coordinates relative to an origin cell, and local IJ coordinates back to H3 cells

Usage

ddbh3_h3_to_local_ij(
  x,
  origin,
  h3 = "h3string",
  new_column = c("i", "j"),
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

ddbh3_local_ij_to_h3(
  x,
  origin,
  i = "i",
  j = "j",
  new_column = "h3cell",
  conn = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  mode = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Input data. One of:

duckspatial_df

A lazy spatial data frame via dbplyr.

sf

A spatial data frame.

tbl_lazy

A lazy data frame from dbplyr.

data.frame

A standard R data frame.

character string

A table or view name in conn.

character vector

A vector of values to operate on in vectorized mode (requires conn = NULL).

origin

The name of a column in x containing the H3 cells used as origin of the local IJ coordinate system

h3

The name of a column in x containing the H3 strings or H3 unsigned 64-bit integers (UBIGINT)

new_column

Name of the new column(s) to create on the input data. For ddbh3_h3_to_local_ij(), a character vector of length 2 with the names of the I and J columns (defaults to c("i", "j")). For ddbh3_local_ij_to_h3(), the name of the cell column (defaults to "h3cell"). If the input already has a column with any of these names, it is replaced by the result

conn

A connection object to a DuckDB database. If NULL, the function runs on a temporary DuckDB database.

name

A character string of length one specifying the name of the table, or a character string of length two specifying the schema and table names. If NULL (the default), the function returns the result as an sf object

mode

Character. Controls the return type. Options:

  • "duckspatial" (default): Lazy spatial data frame backed by dbplyr/DuckDB

  • "sf": Eagerly collected sf object (uses memory)

Can be set globally via ddbs_options(mode = "...") or per-function via this argument. Per-function overrides global setting. It only applies when the output has a geometry column, and is ignored otherwise.

overwrite

Boolean. whether to overwrite the existing table if it exists. Defaults to FALSE. This argument is ignored when name is NULL.

quiet

A logical value. If TRUE, suppresses any informational messages. Defaults to FALSE.

i, j

The names of the columns in x containing the local I and J coordinates

Value

One of the following, depending on the inputs:

tbl_lazy

If the output has no geometry, i.e. x is not spatial and the function adds a column. mode is ignored in this case.

duckspatial_df

If the output has geometry (x is spatial, e.g. an sf or duckspatial_df object, or the function builds geometries, as *_to_spatial() and ddbh3_h3_to_points() do) and mode = "duckspatial" (default).

sf

If the output has geometry and mode = "sf".

TRUE (invisibly)

If name is provided, a table is created in the connection and TRUE is returned invisibly.

vector

If x is a character vector and conn = NULL, the function operates in vectorized mode, returning a vector of the same length as x.

Details

Local IJ coordinates are integer coordinates of a cell in a 2D grid anchored at an origin cell. They are useful to work with cells as a regular grid (e.g. offsets between cells or image-like operations):

  • ddbh3_h3_to_local_ij() adds two integer columns with the I and J coordinates of the cell in h3 relative to the cell in origin

  • ddbh3_local_ij_to_h3() returns the cell at the I and J coordinates relative to the cell in origin. The cell is returned in the same format as origin (string or UBIGINT)

Local IJ coordinates are only defined near the origin: the origin and the cell must have the same resolution and be close enough to each other (and not cross pentagon distortion). Otherwise, the result is NA. The origin is not placed at (0, 0), and the coordinates are only comparable between cells that share the same origin.

Both functions work inside dplyr::mutate(). There, ddbh3_h3_to_local_ij(origin, h3) returns a list column with the [i, j] pair; use ij[[1]] and ij[[2]] to extract each coordinate.

Examples

## Load needed packages
library(duckh3)
library(dplyr)

## Setup the default connection with h3 and spatial extensions
## This is a mandatory step to use duckh3 functions
ddbh3_default_conn(threads = 1)

## Cells within 2 steps of an origin cell
cells_tbl <- data.frame(origin = "88283470a1fffff") |>
  ddbh3_grid_disk(k = 2, h3 = "origin", new_column = "h3string")

## CELLS TO LOCAL IJ ------

## Local IJ coordinates relative to the origin
ij_tbl <- ddbh3_h3_to_local_ij(cells_tbl, origin = "origin")
ij_tbl

## Shift the cells one step along the I axis
ij_tbl |>
  mutate(i = i + 1L) |>
  ddbh3_local_ij_to_h3(origin = "origin", new_column = "h3shifted")

## Inside mutate (`ij[[1]]` extracts the I coordinate)
ij_tbl |>
  mutate(
    ij = ddbh3_h3_to_local_ij(origin, h3string),
    i_mutate = ij[[1]],
    h3cell = ddbh3_local_ij_to_h3(origin, i, j)
  )
